title: Three-dimensional model
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees. Ensure the translation vector is set to zero, zero, and zero. On the first face, draw the first loop consisting of six lines. Start the first line from the origin at zero, zero to zero point zero three three nine, zero. Continue with the second line from zero point zero three three nine, zero to zero point zero three three nine, zero point zero three three nine. Draw the third line from zero point zero three three nine, zero point zero three three nine to zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero three three nine. The fourth line should go from zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero three three nine to zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero zero two. The fifth line extends from zero point zero three one nine, zero point zero zero two to zero, zero point zero zero two. Finally, draw the sixth line back to the origin at zero, zero. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point zero three three nine. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles as before and translate it using the zero vector. Extrude the transformed sketch zero point seven five units in the direction of the normal to create a new solid body. The dimensions of the resulting three-dimensional model are zero point zero three three nine three six six five one five eight three seven one zero four one units in length, zero point zero three three nine three six six five one five eight three seven one zero four one units in width, and zero point seven five units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch points
p1 = (0.0, 0.0)
p2 = (0.0339, 0.0)
p3 = (0.0339, 0.0339)
p4 = (0.0319, 0.0339)
p5 = (0.0319, 0.002)
p6 = (0.0, 0.002)

# Create the sketch
r = r.moveTo(p1[0], p1[1]) \
     .lineTo(p2[0], p2[1]) \
     .lineTo(p3[0], p3[1]) \
     .lineTo(p4[0], p4[1]) \
     .lineTo(p5[0], p5[1]) \
     .lineTo(p6[0], p6[1]) \
     .lineTo(p1[0], p1[1]) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The given Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0339, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0321, 0.0339) \
     .lineTo(0.0321, 0.0018) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0018) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r = r

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# L-shaped angle profile in the YZ plane, extruded along X
# Overall Y size = 0.0339, Z size = 0.0339, length along X = 0.75
leg = 0.0339
thick = 0.0085

r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .polyline([
        (0, 0),
        (leg, 0),
        (leg, thick),
        (thick, thick),
        (thick, leg),
        (0, leg),
    ])
    .close()
    .extrude(0.75)
)

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# L-angle bar: L-shaped cross-section (Y x Z = 0.0339 x 0.0339) extruded along X (0.75)
s = 0.0339   # leg length (outer dimension of the square cross-section)
t = 0.005    # leg wall thickness
L = 0.75     # length along X

# Sketch the L profile on the YZ plane and extrude along +X
r = (
    cq.Workplane("YZ")
    .moveTo(0, 0)
    .lineTo(s, 0)
    .lineTo(s, t)
    .lineTo(t, t)
    .lineTo(t, s)
    .lineTo(0, s)
    .close()
    .extrude(L)
)
